chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I was circumambulating (the Kaaba) and Sufyan al-Thawri was near me, so he said, 'O Abu Abdillah! What did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) do with the Stone when he reached it?' I said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would touch it (istalam) during every obligatory and optional circumambulation.' He said, 'So he stayed behind me a little. When I reached the Stone, I passed by it and walked, but I did not touch it. So he caught up with me and said, 'O Abu Abdillah! Did you not inform me that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to touch the Stone during every obligatory and optional circumambulation?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'But you passed by it and did not touch it.' I said, 'The people showed respect for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that they do not show for me, and whenever he reached the Stone, they would make a way for him until he touched it, and I dislike the congestion (of pushing people).'

key_terms.يَسْتَلِمُهُ: He would touch it (specifically with the hand)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq not touch the Black Stone during every circumambulation if the Prophet did?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the nuanced application of Sunnah by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), who distinguished between the Prophet’s unique honor, where crowds parted for him, and the practical wisdom of avoiding unnecessary crowding (zihama) for the Imams. It serves as a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for understanding that ritual acts are not merely mechanical repetitions but are influenced by social context and the specific status of the actor. The narration underscores the balance between following prophetic precedent and exercising personal discretion (ijtihad) in ritual practice.
